description:
You are a regional operations manager reviewing annual spending across 8 cost centers. The workbook contains two sheets: 'Budget' (approved budget by cost center, expense category, and month for the full year) and 'Actuals' (actual spending for the same structure). Some actuals reflect mid-year changes — a rent increase in May, personnel raises in September, and an unplanned IT purchase in July — that were not in the original budget.

Build a comprehensive budget variance analysis workbook:

1. Add a 'Monthly_Variance' sheet showing for each cost center and category: the budget amount, actual amount, dollar variance (Actual - Budget), and percentage variance for every month. Use formulas referencing the Budget and Actuals sheets.

2. Add a 'YTD_Summary' sheet with year-to-date totals by cost center: YTD Budget, YTD Actual, YTD Variance ($), YTD Variance (%), and a 'Trend' indicator showing whether the variance is improving or worsening compared to the prior quarter.

3. Add an 'Executive_Summary' sheet containing: total company YTD variance, the 3 cost centers with the largest unfavorable variances (use LARGE and INDEX-MATCH), the 3 expense categories with the largest favorable variances, and the percentage of line items that are over budget.

4. Apply conditional formatting to the Monthly_Variance sheet: red background for unfavorable variances > 5%, green for favorable variances > 5%, icon sets (arrows) on the YTD_Summary Trend column.

5. Create two charts: a clustered bar chart on the YTD_Summary sheet comparing YTD Budget vs YTD Actual by cost center, and a line chart on the Executive_Summary sheet showing monthly total variance trend across all 12 months.

Save the completed workbook.

metadata.industry: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
metadata.data_source: Operational budget and actuals data modeled on real mid-market company departmental spending patterns with realistic mid-year adjustments
